importance: Builds baby's cells and reduces risk of birth defects such as spina bifida
food_sources: Green leafy vegetables; Fruit; Wholegrain breads and cereals; Fortified breakfast cereals; Legumes; Nuts
when_to_take: When planning pregnancy and continue for first 3 months of pregnancy
special_considerations: Higher dose may be needed for family history of cleft lip/spinal problems, anti-epilepsy medication, or Type 1/Type 2 diabetes

food_sources: Fish (1-3 times per week, limit high mercury types); Iodised salt
supplement_dose: At least 150 micrograms per day in pregnancy multivitamin
special_considerations: Do NOT take kelp (seaweed) tablets - may contain too much iodine

food_sources: Meat; Chicken; Fish; Eggs; Dairy foods; Nuts; Legumes (dried beans and lentils); Tofu
special_considerations: Also helps iron and calcium intake

importance: Makes red blood cells that carry oxygen. Volume of blood increases during pregnancy and baby's blood is developing
food_sources: Meat, chicken, fish (at least 2 serves daily); Legumes; Nuts; Wholegrain breads and cereals; Green leafy vegetables; Vitamin C-rich foods (eaten with plant iron sources to boost absorption)
supplement_required: If blood tests show low levels
special_considerations: Eat vitamin C-rich foods with plant iron sources to boost absorption

food_sources: Dairy foods (low fat has same calcium as full fat); Fish with edible bones (canned salmon, sardines); Firm tofu; Calcium-fortified plant milks (at least 100mg per 100ml)
supplement_required: If not eating dairy or calcium-fortified alternatives
special_considerations: Need 2-3 serves of calcium-rich foods daily

importance: Important for development of baby's bones and teeth. Low levels can cause muscle weakness/pain in women and rickets in babies
food_sources: Sunlight (mostly made in skin); Oily fish; Egg yolks; Margarine; Some brands of milk
special_considerations: Higher dose needed if blood test shows deficiency

importance: Needed for healthy brain, nerve and eye development in baby
food_sources: Fish (especially oily fish: tuna, salmon, sardines, mackerel); Walnuts; Chia seeds; Linseeds (flax seeds); Soybeans
supplement_required: Optional - some pregnancy multivitamins include it
special_considerations: Avoid fish liver oils (too much vitamin A). Limit high-mercury fish.

supplement_required: Yes - for vegetarians/vegans who don't eat animal foods
when_to_take: Throughout pregnancy if not eating animal products
